reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's How Supersmart Ate the Elephant and its frame (the monkey advising the crocodile); all four encounters and the tactic used in each are kept in order.
The closing verses, including one about Brahmans and women, are omitted with disclosure; the elephant made old is disclosed after review.
Age band 8+: no one is killed in the story (the elephant has already died); the rival is bitten and chased off with no wound described, and the trickery goes unpunished, as the content note says.
Natural Kannada with real dialogue; the pause question comes before the false alarm. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; one Codex gpt-5.6-sol generation with seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text.
The dead elephant is drawn only as a peaceful grey shape lying with its eyes closed, read as a grey hill; no wound, meat or blood anywhere.

Fixed before approval: the jackal had an extra human-like arm in panels 3 and 5; one edit pass removed it so it has four canine legs, and only those panels were composited back. Alt texts for scenes 3, 5 and 6 were corrected to match the pictures.
The lion, tiger, leopard and the rival jackal are distinct and consistent; the rival is only chased, never bitten in the picture.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by a separate agent.
